Etonogestrel, in turn, binds to Esr1, indicating a direct interaction between the compound and the receptor. The lowest common ancestor of these entities is the 3-Oxo-Delta(4) Steroid, suggesting a shared biochemical pathway. The integration of these pathways implies that Progesterone may influence Esr1 through Etonogestrel, potentially via a mechanism involving steroid hormone signaling. The evidence supports a causal link between Progesterone and Esr1 through the intermediary of Etonogestrel, highlighting a possible role in hormonal regulation.
